\section[o agente]{o agente — the officer, the agent}

\label{lesson:PT-C293-agente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the fugitive, then the Portuguese for the chase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o agente}
\textbf{o agente} — \textquotedblleft{}the officer, the agent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Um agente da polícia ajudou-nos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A police officer helped us.}
\end{quote}

The polite way to address a police officer: \emph{Sim, senhor agente}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{agente} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{agēns} \textquotedblleft{}doing, acting\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{agere} \textquotedblleft{}to do, to drive\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o agente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o agente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o agente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the fugitive, then the Portuguese for the chase, then say \emph{o agente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o agente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The officer, the agent\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a patrulha]{a patrulha — the patrol}

\label{lesson:PT-C293-patrulha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the chase, then the Portuguese for the officer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a patrulha}
\textbf{a patrulha} — \textquotedblleft{}the patrol\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Uma patrulha passa pela rua todas as noites.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A patrol goes down the street every night.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Um carro de patrulha} — a patrol car.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{patrulha} was borrowed from French \emph{patrouille} \textquotedblleft{}a patrol\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a patrulha}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the chase, then the Portuguese for the officer, then say \emph{a patrulha} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[patrulhar]{patrulhar — to patrol}

\label{lesson:PT-C293-patrulhar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the officer, then the Portuguese for the patrol.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: patrulhar}
\textbf{patrulhar} — \textquotedblleft{}to patrol\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os polícias patrulham o bairro de bicicleta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The police patrol the neighbourhood by bike.}
\end{quote}

Takes a direct object: \emph{patrulhar a costa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{patrulhar} was borrowed from French \emph{patrouiller}, first \textquotedblleft{}to paddle about in mud\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}to patrol\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{patte} \textquotedblleft{}a paw\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patrulhar}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the officer, then the Portuguese for the patrol, then say \emph{patrulhar} again

\section[vigiar]{vigiar — to keep watch over, to guard}

\label{lesson:PT-C293-vigiar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the patrol, then the Portuguese for to patrol.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: vigiar}
\textbf{vigiar} — \textquotedblleft{}to keep watch over, to guard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O meu pai vigia as crianças na praia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My father keeps an eye on the children at the beach.}
\end{quote}

Also of the police: \emph{vigiar uma casa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vigiar} comes down from Old Portuguese (EtymDB) and goes back to Latin \emph{vigilāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stay awake, to keep watch\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{vigiar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the patrol, then the Portuguese for to patrol, then say \emph{vigiar} again
\end{itemize}

\section[a vigilância]{a vigilância — surveillance, watch}

\label{lesson:PT-C293-vigilancia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to patrol, then the Portuguese for to keep watch over.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a vigilância}
\textbf{a vigilância} — \textquotedblleft{}surveillance, watch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O museu tem vigilância dia e noite.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The museum is watched day and night.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Câmaras de vigilância} — security cameras.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vigilância} was borrowed from Latin \emph{vigilantia} \textquotedblleft{}wakefulness, watchfulness\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{vigilāre} \textquotedblleft{}to keep watch\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
